item: The launcher evidence files (exits, stops, stderr; bash and PowerShell) never lose a row to another launcher (R173)
summary: Measured with 8 launchers at once and the file seeded so the trim fires: bash exit rows 8 of 96 lost, stop rows 69 of 96 (files left with 0 and 1 lines), PowerShell exit rows 4 of 48 with 2 torn lines, and a live launcher lost all 3 of its stderr rows when two later launchers started under it (the awk filter held the file open across another launcher's rename-trim). Now every append and trim of one file runs under one lock per file (flock, else a mkdir lock holding the owner pid so a dead owner's lock is taken over; a named Mutex in PowerShell), a trim writes a temp name of its own, the filter appends one row at a time through the same locked append (handed the helper source to eval: an exported function did not reach the one-true-awk's shell and lost every row with close status 0), and a failed PowerShell append no longer switches later rows off. A wait that runs out costs the TRIM, never the row. The wait is the longest measured append+trim hold, rounded up: bash 30 ms (27.3 ms over 320 calls), PowerShell 150 ms (144.9 ms over 96, cold), pinned by a test. After: 0 lost in the same runs (bash 32+32 rows, PowerShell 48), 0 torn; no bytes change. PowerShell 5.1, a real Windows console and named-mutex behaviour on real Windows were never run; the PowerShell race test is probabilistic on the base (red in some runs, not all). Zips from launchers before this carry the caveat in the triage header.
